title: Why AI Coding Agents Crash at 3 AM: The Happy-Path Mirage & The Forced Continuity Defect
why_read: A heavily stylized blog post with grandiose framing about AI coding agent failures that reads more like rhetoric than substantive technical analysis.
analysis: The piece uses dramatic narrative devices (a fabricated Randal Schwartz quote, '3 AM' framing) to discuss why LLM-based coding agents fail in production under real-world conditions like network latency and race conditions. While the underlying observation that agents fail to handle non-happy-path conditions is valid and relevant, the excerpt is long on evocative storytelling and short on concrete technical detail or evidence. It reads as opinion/thought-leadership content rather than a rigorous technical breakdown.
